sections.h2: Harrison County and who taxes property there
sections.html:
Harrison County is in north-central West Virginia, with Clarksburg as its seat. Bridgeport, Clarksburg, Salem, Shinnston, Stonewood, Anmoore, Lumberport, Nutter Fort and West Milford are among its incorporated places, and Interstate 79 runs through the county. Four bodies bill against a Harrison County parcel: the state, the county commission, the county board of education and, inside a municipality, the city or town.

Housing demand leans on health care, federal employment and offices along I-79. United Hospital Center and the FBI's Criminal Justice Information Services Division are among the larger employers. A big employer does not fix an individual house with a failing roof or a tenant problem, though. Sellers with those issues still price against what a buyer will pay after repairs.

sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
Valuing is the assessor's job and collecting is the sheriff's. You will find both inside the General Services Building, 229 South Third Street, Clarksburg.

QuestionPhone
Assessor's Office, general304-624-8510
Taxes due (how much you owe)304-624-8685
Homestead exemptions304-624-8540
Mobile home assessments304-624-8517
Oil and gas and minerals division304-624-8523

The assessor's site lists separate numbers for individual and business assessments as well. The office posts summer satellite days at places such as Meadowbrook Mall, the Clarksburg Senior Center and several fire stations, so people in Shinnston, Lost Creek or Spelter do not always need to drive downtown. Filing is also available online through the state's SmartFile system.

sections.h2: Filing dates and the homestead exemption
sections.html:
The assessor's 2026 filing season runs from July 1, and the dates differ by form. Individuals have until October 1 to file personal property returns, starting July 1. Businesses, along with anyone seeking the farm exemption, must file by September 1. A homestead application is accepted July 1 through December 1 and starts with the next tax year.

Tickets run on the state calendar. Expect yours from July 15 onward, with installments due September 1 and March 1 and a 2.5 percent discount for paying ahead of either. Interest of 9 percent a year starts once the first half is past October 1, or the second half past April 1.

Under the homestead exemption, $20,000 of assessed value drops off the bill for a resident owner aged 65 or over, or certified permanently and totally disabled. If that is you, double-check that the paperwork was filed, since a lapse inflates the bill on the house you are selling.

Begin with a conversation at the Assessor's Office. Still unhappy? Present your case to the county commissioners, who serve as the Board of Equalization and Review from February 1 until February 28. The board can reduce a value that exceeds 60 percent of true and actual value, and it must give written notice at least five days before raising one.

Losing at the board sends you to the Office of Tax Appeals, where a petition must be in by March 31 of the tax year. Missing the February window waives the right to argue that year's list. A dispute over whether a home is Class II or Class IV is handled separately with the assessor and the Tax Commissioner.

Good evidence is concrete: a recent appraisal, a repair estimate for a damaged structure, or sales of similar homes. If you plan to sell soon, an appeal is often not worth the effort unless the value is clearly wrong, because the new owner will be assessed on the next cycle anyway.

sections.h2: Unpaid tax and a cash sale
sections.html:
The sheriff certifies unpaid real estate tax for sale, and the State Auditor, not the sheriff, now runs the lien sale. The certification deadline is October 31. Call the Sheriff at 304-624-8685 before you assume anything about timing or redemption cost.

A seller who owes tax can often clear it through closing. Your title company requests the payoff and settles it from proceeds. Recording a deed also draws a county excise tax of 55 cents on each $500 of value.

We buy houses in Harrison County as-is, so a house in Clarksburg that needs a roof, has a tenant, or carries back taxes does not need to be fixed first. For a written cash offer, call or text (424) 435-2326.

sections.h2: Minerals, mobile homes and property classes
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office keeps separate divisions for mobile homes and for oil, gas and minerals. A mobile home may be assessed through its own desk at 304-624-8517, and oil and gas or mineral matters go to 304-624-8523. The state also runs its own appraisal process for oil and gas royalties.

Before closing, ask both the assessor and the title company if a mineral interest rides with the parcel and is assessed separately. Deeds do not always say, and a buyer will want a clear answer. Cash buyers are generally fine with houses where title questions like this need work, and we check before we make an offer.

West Virginia's four classes matter too. Class II means a home that the owner lives in and uses only as a residence. Property in a municipality that does not qualify, such as a rental house in Clarksburg, falls in Class IV, and property outside a municipality falls in Class III. Those classes have higher regular ceilings than Class II.

sections.h2: Timeline for a sale with open tax
sections.html:
Think of the process in four steps. In week one, request the amount due from the sheriff's taxes-due line and ask whether any mobile home or mineral piece is assessed apart from the house. Next, gather the deed and any estate papers. Then choose a closing date that does not fall right as a delinquency date passes, since interest at 9 percent a year keeps building. Finally, the title company pays everything owed at the table.

Calling the Assessor's Office early also lets you learn whether you can use a satellite day in your area rather than driving to Clarksburg.

A quick checklist helps before you list. Dial 304-624-8685 to learn what each ticket owes. Then ask the Assessor's Office for the house's class and whether a homestead exemption is on file. Check whether a mobile home or mineral interest has its own assessment. Hand everything to the title company so payoff and deed tax are set well before closing day.

If the taxes are old, the house needs work, or heirs have not agreed, a sale for cash skips much of the waiting. Taxes owed are still paid out of your proceeds by the title company, and repair bills and showings drop away.

faqs.q: What are the Harrison County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: One half is due September 1 and the other March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for paying early. After October 1 (first half) or April 1 (second half) the unpaid amount is delinquent and gains 9 percent interest yearly.

faqs.q: Where is the Harrison County Sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 229 South 3rd Street, Clarksburg, WV 26301, and the phone for taxes due is 304-624-8685. Online payment is also offered.

faqs.q: When can I apply for the homestead exemption in Harrison County?
faqs.a: Filing opens July 1 and closes December 1, and the exemption then takes effect the next tax year. Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, get $20,000 off assessed value.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Harrison County assessment?
faqs.a: Protest in person before the county commission acting as the Board of Equalization and Review between February 1 and February 28. Going further to the Office of Tax Appeals requires a March 31 filing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Harrison County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask a title company to pull the payoff on the overdue tax, and it will be paid from your proceeds when the sale closes.
